newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Bursodchem signs MDI expansion with Mitsui.
newsitem.headline: Bursodchem signs MDI expansion with Mitsui.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals company Borsodchem Rt said on Thursday it had signed a deal with Japan's Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals and Chisso Engineering on the expansion of its MDI capacity to 40,000 tonnes per year.
"The value of the deal would be inside two billion forints," Borsodchem CEO Laszlo Kovacs told Reuters.
He added, that the increased capacity would come on line in September 1998, after the annual August repair pause.
Borsodchem's current MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate) capacity is 32,500 tonnes per year.
Although its output volume is much smaller than that of Borsodchem's other main product, PVC, MDI last year accounted for 40 percent of the company's profits.
Increased MDI capacity also hedges the company against the PVC price cycle, the company and analysts said earlier.

Borsodchem last year increased its MDI capacity to 32,500 tonnes per year from 25,000 tonnes per year, with an investment of 1.3 billion forints. That upgrade was also carried out by Japan's Mitsui which licensed the technology to Borsodchem.
Borsodchem had a net profit of 5.80 billion forints on net sales of 43.65 billion forints in 1996 versus 6.09 billion forints net profit on net sales of 41.34 billion in 1995.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Borsodchem shares closed at 6,350 forints, down 70.
